summary: The note compares intramural sports with varsity athletics at local colleges, weighing time commitment, competition level, skills, networking, and health benefits. Intramurals are flexible and inclusive, while varsity demands heavy time and offers prestige and scholarship opportunities. It concludes there is no one-size-fits-all answer; the choice depends on personal priorities.
one_line: A comparative look at whether college students should invest their time in flexible intramural sports or demanding varsity athletics.
key_facts: Wesleyan College's intramural soccer league opens October 15, 2023 with a ceremony headlined by alumnus and former professional player Jenna Martin.
Jamison Hurd, captain of Easton University's basketball team, commits upwards of 20 hours per week to varsity play.
Varsity sports involve multiple training sessions per week plus travel and competition at least every weekend, and can lead to athletic scholarships.
Easton University's football team scouted high schools on September 10 before the varsity league's commencement on October 1.
Laura Schmidt, a senior at Midtown Liberal Arts College, does both varsity track and field and intramural badminton, saying intramurals offer balance for academically serious students.
Intramural leagues often play once or twice a week and require minimal travel time.
Thompson College's intramural basketball league, which began September 18, has participation from over 20% of the student body.
Alberto Gomez, a varsity swimmer at Riverside University, said "The pressure to perform academically and athletically can become overwhelming."
Sarah Jennings, a former varsity rower and graduate assistant at City Central College, believes varsity sports build unrivaled teamwork, leadership, and discipline skills.
Tom Anderson organizes the Homecoming Intramural Flag Football event at Valley State University on November 5, describing it as cross-pollination between majors and class years.
The 2nd Annual Wellness Week at Brookfield Institute starts November 12 and includes panels on how both levels of sport affect mental health and stress reduction.
Rebecca Liu, an intramural volleyball player at Greenwood Community College, found intramurals less intimidating than varsity tryouts while still growing as an athlete.
